t: Philip IV succeeds Philip III as Spanish king
c: Philip III was succeeded in 1621 by his son Philip IV.

t: Cardinal Richelieu declares France at war with Spain
c: Sweden lost and France's First Minister, Cardinal Richelieu, in 1635 declared war on Spain.

t: Portugal and Catalonia rebel against Spanish rule
c: In 1640, both Portugal and Catalonia rebelled.

t: Dutch capture 's-Hertogenbosch and Wesel
c: The Dutch won very easily at 's-Hertogenbosch and Wesel in 1629.

t: Dutch capture strategic fortress town of Maastricht
c: In 1632 the Dutch captured the strategic fortress town of Maastricht, repulsing three relief armies and dooming the Spanish to defeat.

t: Seville's textile industry drastically declines
c: Industry went into reverse – Seville in 1621 operated 400 looms, where it had 16,000 a century before.

t: Philip V orders invasion of Sardinia
c: In 1717, Philip V ordered an invasion of Sardinia.

t: Spain reconquers Naples and Sicily
c: Later, however, Spain reconquered Naples and Sicily during the War of the Polish Succession.

t: Spain obtains Italian duchies
c: In 1748, after the War of the Austrian Succession, Spain obtained the duchies of Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla in northern Italy.

c: After 1814, as Napoleon was defeated and Ferdinand VII was back on the throne, the king sent armies to regain control and reimpose autocratic rule.

t: Liberal Triennium begins in Spain
c: This was the start of the second bourgeois revolution in Spain, the trienio liberal which lasted from 1820 to 1823.

t: Congress of Verona authorizes French intervention
c: The liberal government was viewed with hostility by the Congress of Verona in 1822, and France was authorized to intervene.

t: Queen Regent María Christina resigns, Espartero becomes regent
c: The Queen Regent preferred to resign and let Espartero become regent instead in 1840.

t: General O'Donnell leads pronunciamiento
c: There was another pronunciamiento in 1854 led General Leopoldo O'Donnell, intending to topple the discredited rule of the Count of San Luis.

c: A popular insurrection followed the coup and the Progressive Party obtained widespread support in Spain and came to government in 1854.

t: Cortes declares Spain will have a king
c: Two years later, in 1870, the Cortes declared that Spain would again have a king.

t: First Spanish Republic faces multiple threats
c: The First Spanish Republic was immediately under siege from all quarters.

t: Alfonso XIII begins reign after regency
c: The reign of Alfonso was followed by that of his son Alfonso XIII, initially a regency until the latter's coming of age in 1902.

t: Cuba launches war of independence
c: In 1868, Cuba launched a war of independence against Spain.

t: Spanish republic proclaimed after king flees
c: The king fled the country and a republic was proclaimed on 14 April 1931.

t: Popular Front elected to power in Spain
c: In 1936, the Left united in the Popular Front and were elected to power.

t: Thousands of Republicans imprisoned and executed
c: After the war, many thousands of Republicans were imprisoned and up to 150,000 were executed between 1939 and 1943.

t: Spanish Guinea granted independence as Equatorial Guinea
c: Spanish Guinea was granted independence as Equatorial Guinea in 1968, while the Moroccan enclave of Ifni had been ceded to Morocco in 1969.

t: Partido Popular government elected under José María Aznar
c: In 1996, the centre-right Partido Popular government came to power, led by José María Aznar.

c: During the Iron Age, considered the protohistory of the territory, Celts came, in several waves, possibly starting before 600 BC.

t: Decimus Junius Brutus leads expedition to Gallaecia
c: Between 135 and 132 BC, Consul Decimus Junius Brutus brought about an expedition to Gallaecia (north of Portugal and Galicia).

c: Hamilcar was succeeded by Hasdrubal the Fair, his son-in-law, in 226 BC.

t: Hasdrubal marches army along Iberian coast
c: In 217 BC, Hasdrubal marched his army along the coast while his ships sailed near the shore.

t: Mago Barca prepares forces to march to Italy
c: In 215 BC, Mago Barca, Hannibal's brother, was preparing to go to Italy with a force of 12,000 infantry, 1,500 cavalry, 20 elephants and 60 warships.

t: Mago and Hasdrubal rout Hispanic force
c: In 214 BC, Mago and Hasdrubal routed a large Hispanic force.

t: Syphax of Masaesyli rebels against Carthage
c: In 213 BC, Syphax, king of the Masaesyli of western Numidia (Algeria), rebelled against Carthage.

t: The Scipios join forces to end the war
c: In 212 BC, the two Scipios joined their forces and agreed that it was time for a push to end the war.

t: Roman Senate sends Gaius Nero to Hispania
c: In 211 BC, the Roman senate sent Gaius Nero to Hispania with 6,000 Roman and 6,000 allied infantry and 300 Roman and 600 allied cavalry.

t: Scipio and Silanus command extended in Hispania
c: In 209 BC, the command of Publius Cornelius Scipio and Marcus Junius Silanus was extended.

t: Gaius Cornelius Cethegus defeats Sedetani forces
c: He arrived in 200 BC.

c: In 196 BC, Hispania Ulterior was assigned to Quintus Fabius Buteo and Hispania Citerior to Quintus Minucius Thermus.

c: In 194 BC, the praetors Publius Cornelius Scipio Nasica and Sextus Digitus were assigned Hispania Ulterior and Citerior respectively.

t: Lucius Aemilius Paulus replaces Marcus Fulvius Nobilitor
c: In 191 BC, the term Gaius Flaminius was extended and Lucius Aemilius Paulus replaced Marcus Fulvius Nobilitor in Hispania Ulterior.

t: Publius Junius Brutus and Lucius Plautius Hypsaeus appointed praetors
c: In 189 BC, Publius Junius Brutus and Lucius Plautius Hypsaeus were the praetors of Hispania Ulterior and Citerior respectively.

t: Marcus Cornelius Scipio Maluginensis and Publius Licinius Crassus appointed
c: In 176 BC, Marcus Cornelius Scipio Maluginensis and Publius Licinius Crassus were assigned Hispania Ulterior and Citerior respectively.

t: Marcus Junius and Spurius Lucretius assigned to provinces
c: In 172 BC, Marcus Junius and Spurius Lucretius were assigned Hispania Citerior and Ulterior respectively.

t: Lucius Canuleius Dives allocated Hispania
c: In 171 BC, it was allocated to Lucius Canuleius Dives.

t: Publius Fonteius assigned to Hispania
c: In 168 BC, Hispania was assigned to Publius Fonteius.

t: Two provinces reconstituted in Hispania
c: In 167 BC, after the Third Macedonian War it was decided to reconstitute two provinces in Hispania.

t: Marcus Claudius Marcellus takes command in Hispania
c: In 152 BC, Marcus Claudius Marcellus, consul for the third time, took over the command, bringing 8,000 infantry and 500 cavalry to Hispania.

t: Marcus Claudius Marcellus replaces Nobilior
c: Nobilior was replaced in the following year (152 BC) by Marcus Claudius Marcellus (consul 166 BC).

t: Lucius Licinius Lucullus succeeds Marcellus
c: He in turn was succeeded in 150 BC by Lucius Licinius Lucullus, who was distinguished by his cruelty and infamy.

t: Viriathus leads Lusitanian rebellion against Romans
c: In 147 BC, a new Lusitanian leader named Viriathus rebelled against the Roman forces.

t: Viriathus assassinated by Audax, Ditalcus and Minurus
c: Viriathus was assassinated about 139 BC by Audax, Ditalcus and Minurus, probably paid off by the Roman General Marcus Popillius Laenas.

t: Quintus Caecilius Metellus Macedonicus subdues the Arevaci
c: In 143 BC, the consul Quintus Caecilius Metellus Macedonicus subdued the Arevaci by attacking them suddenly while they were harvesting.

t: Quintus Pompeius Aulus takes command in Hispania
c: In 142 BC, the praetor Quintus Pompeius Aulus took over with a well-trained army of 30,000 infantry and 2,000 cavalry.

t: Marcus Popillius Laenas arrives as new consul
c: In 139 BC, when the new consul, Marcus Popillius Laenas, arrived to take over, the last instalment was being paid.

t: Gaius Hostilius Mancinus loses battles with Numantines
c: In 137 BC, the consul Gaius Hostilius Mancinus lost frequent clashes with the Numantines.

t: Titus Didius sent to Hispania
c: In 98 BC, after the defeat of the Cimbri, the consul Titus Didius was sent to Hispania.

t: Celtiberian rebellion erupts
c: In 82 BC, there was a Celtiberian rebellion.

t: Titus Didius celebrates triumph in Rome
c: He did not return to Rome until his triumph in 93 BC.

t: Valerius Flaccus celebrates triumph in Rome
c: Valerius Flaccus returned to Rome for his triumph in 81 BC, which was awarded for his actions in both Celtiberia and Gallia Narbonensis.

t: Sertorian War begins in Hispania
c: This civil war was fought in Hispania between Quintus Sertorius in coalition with native tribes and the regime of Sulla from 80 BC to 72 BC.

t: Sertorius defeats Aurelius Cotta's naval force
c: In 80 BC, Sertorius defeated a naval force under Aurelius Cotta and landed in Hispania.

t: Caecilius Metellus defeats Lucius Hirtuleius
c: In 75 BC, Caecilius Metellus defeated and killed Lucius Hirtuleius.
